lesson.title: Handle changed roles and supplier dependence: case exercise
lesson.summary: Reassign provider duties after changes and secure necessary supplier assistance.

prerequisites.reason: The consequence is a new allocation of provider obligations.

blocks: **Changed provider role** under Article 25 can arise for distributors, importers, deployers or others that rebrand an existing high-risk system, substantially modify one so it remains high-risk, or change a non-high-risk system’s intended purpose so it becomes high-risk.

Substantial modification is an unplanned post-assessment change affecting requirement compliance or changing assessed purpose. Rebranding has the stated contractual-allocation qualification. Section A safety-component product manufacturers also become providers in the specified own-name supply/service circumstances.

For the specific changed system, the initial provider is no longer its provider under the paragraph. It must closely cooperate with the new provider, supply necessary information and reasonably expected assistance, including relevant documentation, limitations/failure modes and targeted testing access.

The cooperation paragraph does not apply where the initial provider clearly specified the system must not be changed into a high-risk system. Do not assume the new provider can compel support under this route regardless of that boundary.

A **supplier-access agreement** specifies in writing necessary information, capabilities, technical access and other assistance from third-party systems/models/tools/services/components/processes for the high-risk provider to comply, based on the generally acknowledged state of the art.

The exception for publicly accessible free/open-source tools/services/processes/components excludes general-purpose AI models. A general-purpose model serves many distinct tasks: open licensing does not automatically remove it from this agreement rule. IP, confidential information and trade secrets remain protected.

The AI Office may develop voluntary model contract terms; verify availability before relying on a supposed standard contract. A signed generic purchase contract without needed information/access is not automatically a sufficient agreement.

Case: a customer converts a general writing assistant into materially influential recruitment ranking. Assume the exact Annex III route is established. Its changed purpose triggers a fresh provider-role analysis, not only an employer-use label.

The **value-chain case** asks who now supplies the changed high-risk system and what evidence/access it needs. Preserve applicable importer and corrective duties; a role change does not make all other activities irrelevant.

Record new-provider responsibilities, upstream cooperation conditions, written assistance scope and unresolved access. If the original supplier forbade high-risk conversion, keep the support gap explicit. Do not declare readiness without a route to necessary evidence.
